newsitem.title: FRANCE: French public TV channel lost 199 mln Ffr in 1996.
newsitem.headline: French public TV channel lost 199 mln Ffr in 1996.

text.p: France 2, the biggest French public television channel, said on Wednesday it had a net loss of 199.3 million francs ($33.6 million) in 1996 compared with a net profit of 60.7 million francs in 1995.
It said in a statement the loss was due to extra spending on programmes due to a higher quota of television films it was required to co-produce, and to higher provisions than in 1995.
There was also exceptional spending on coverage of the Olympic Games and the European football championship in the year, the public channel said.
The loss is much bigger than a forecast 70 million franc loss carried in a report last month in Le Monde newspaper on the finances of French public television stations.

The report said France 2 and all the other French public channels, general channel France 3 and specialist stations La Sept, La Cinquieme and Arte, would show losses for 1996, but the financial situation at France 2 was the worst, with a 1996 loss of at least 70 million francs.
France 2 declined comment at the time, saying the accounts for the year had not yet been completed.
The public channel's budget for 1996 was set at 4.88 billion francs, while net receipts came to 4.49 billion, up 2.6 percent from 1995, its statement said.
The government contributed 2.35 billion francs, down 1.6 percent from its 1995 contribution. The remainder of France 2's 1996 receipts came from advertising revenues.
"The initial budget did not allow us to cover extra investment requirements for programmes, notably linked to the rise in the production quota to 16 percent from 15 percent," France 2 said.
"This imbalance, foreseen from the beginning, continued without being remedied by cost saving efforts undertaken by the channel," it said.

France's public television channels were victims of budget austerity under the previous centre-right government, but some commentators expect the new left-wing government to give them more financial support.
France 2 executives have said publicly that extra public funding would give the channel a competitive edge in programming. ($ = 5.936 French Francs)
